subject: MAP: Concurrency stress playtest & tuned-rate recommendations
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeretail.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: MAP kickoff + performance targets (Acme MAP v4)

Rishi / Karthik —

Thanks for the MAP draft (v4). We reviewed the targets with platform and procurement: primary asks below so we can align the playtest earlier next week.

- Latency: <= 250ms P50 and <= 700ms P95 for 32 token completions (avg payload).
- TTFT: <= 120ms for streamed first token on cold connections.
- Throughput: sustain 6k tokens/sec aggregate per region for peak windows.
- Concurrency: burst handling up to 512 concurrent connections for short windows (60s), steady-state target 128 conns.

Open questions: do you expect queueing beyond 100 concurrent requests? What rate-limit settings would you recommend for our front-tier?

We also attached the updated MAP doc (acme_map_v4.pdf) with the proposed close timeline — target close 2027-07-01 pending performance acceptance.

Can we run the playtest Wed → Fri (short bursts on Wed/Thu, 24h soak on Fri)?

—Jordan
Head of Platform, Acme Retail

Attachments: acme_map_v4.pdf (MAP schedule, acceptance criteria)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + performance targets (Acme MAP v4)

Jordan —

Thanks, this is clear and actionable. We can run the schedule you proposed. Quick notes and what we'll deliver in the playtest:

1) Test plan (deliverable): short-burst matrix + nominal steady-state + 24h soak. Will capture p50/p95, TTFT, tokens/sec, and queue depth over time.

2) Concurrency approach: we'll exercise connection-level (many short-lived) and session-level (long-lived with streaming). For burst windows we'll inject using our burst harness (1s ramps up to target). For steady-state we'll cap client connections and shape at target TPS.

3) Rate-limit proposal (initial): per-connection token/sec cap + global leaky-bucket on the gateway. For your profile we recommend start at 60 TPS per connection with a global soft-cap at 6k TPS and hard cap at 7.5k TPS to absorb short spikes. We'll tune after first day of bursts.

4) Observability: we'll share a CSV with time-series metrics and a short summary slide. Karthik will include queueing histograms and backpressure markers.

Next steps:
- Karthik: run dry-run today (Wed) against staging (no throttles) and share initial telemetry.
- Neha: schedule a 30m sync Fri 11:00 ET for results review and close checklist.

I'll attach the test harness config after the dry-run.

—Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + performance targets (Acme MAP v4) — playtest results attached

Team —

We completed the planned playtests (bursts on Wed/Thu; 24h steady-state soak Thu→Fri). Summary highlights (full CSV attached: concurrency_playtest_results.csv):

- Test matrix: concurrency levels 1, 8, 32, 128, 256, 512. Burst windows: 60s ramps; steady-state durations: 24h run at 128 conns.

- Latency (32-token completions): P50 = 180ms, P95 = 560ms at steady-state 128 conns. During 512 burst peaks we observed elevated P95 spikes to ~1.2s for ~30s windows.

- TTFT (streamed first token): median 95ms; 95th 210ms. Cold-connection TTFT averaged 135ms when underlying TLS handshake ran on fresh nodes.

- Throughput: sustained 6.1k TPS regionally during steady-state. Burst peak delivered 7.9k TPS for ~20s before queueing increased.

- Queueing behavior: when the aggregate input exceeded the soft global cap (configured at 6.9k TPS during this run), internal request queue depth rose rapidly and request latencies moved to the tail. We saw request queuing depth up to 3.4k backlog entries in the most extreme burst test. Retries from the client caused transient 429s from the gateway when the hard cap reached.

- Failure modes observed: 429 saturation during sustained bursts combined with client-side aggressive retry (no jitter). Also transient CPU saturation on the oldest GPU fleet nodes (cold-starty kernel warmup).

Recommended tuned-rate settings and mitigations:
1) Gateway soft cap: 6,200 TPS — keeps steady-state within SLO and provides headroom for short spikes.
2) Gateway hard cap: 8,000 TPS — enforces a short window upper bound; rely on client-side backoff.
3) Per-connection cap: 60 TPS (as Rishi suggested). For long-lived streaming clients reduce to 20 TPS equivalent pacing.
4) Client recommendations: add jittered exponential backoff and a retry budget (3 attempts) with per-request timeout of 5s for user-facing calls.
5) Server-side: enable KV-prefix caching for common prompts to shave ~15–25% off P50 under cache hits. Warm new nodes with microbursts prior to put into rotation to avoid kernel cold penalties.

Action items and MAP close timeline update:
- Immediate: we pushed tuned gateway caps (soft 6200 / hard 8000) to your staging for another quick run (today).
- 24h soak: recommend another 24h soak with client backoffs enabled before final acceptance.
- Close target: if soak looks good, move to acceptance review Tue 2027-06-22 and aim to sign by 2027-06-29.

Attachments: concurrency_playtest_results.csv, rate_limit_tuning_notebook.ipynb (notebook with plots and the exact harness config).

—Karthik
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + performance targets (Acme MAP v4) — playtest results attached

Karthik / Rishi —

Really useful — thank you. A few quick notes from platform:
- We'll enable client jitter/backoff today and run the extra 24h soak.
- On the P95 spike during the 512 burst: acceptable as long as we see it subside when soft cap engages (your notes match our tolerance).
- Please add a short section to the MAP doc listing the final tuned caps and the retry guidance (so procurement sees the negotiated limits).

Neha — can you lock a 30m acceptance review Tue 06/22 11:00 ET? Rishi — if we pass the soak, we'll start procurement paperwork that afternoon.

Next: send short summary slide for procurement (one pager).

—Jordan
Head of Platform, Acme Retail
